source.opening_commit_message:
Add image meta to libvirt XML metadata

This patch adds the image_meta used to launch an instance to
the Nova metadata in the libvirt metadata XML.

Nova exposes the image_meta structure when publishing instance
notifications. Downstream services that consume these notifications
such as Ceilometer use this to provide metadata about the image
originally used to create an ephemeral instance or instance
boot volume.

Ceilometer also polls the running instances using the Compute Agent
by reading the metadata of active instances from the libvirt socket.

Adding the data stored in image_meta to the libvirt metadata allows
Ceilometer to discover and expose the actual image metadata used to
launch instances using its compute pollsters, without performing
additional API queries to Nova, Cinder and Glance to get this
information (and even if that was done, it could be different to what
is actually running if images are updated after the fact).

Depending on the type instance, the behaviour of the metadata is:

* Instance built from image => baseImageRef set to the image ID,
  image meta added to the XML
* Instance launched from volume built from image =>
  baseImageRef empty, image meta added to the XML
* Instance launched from volume NOT built from image =>
  baseImageRef empty, no attributes from image meta defined

Change-Id: I09f4f76fff30f9cccf35f4832b9c870095c380ad
source.subject: Add image meta to libvirt XML metadata

targets.commit_message:
Publish image meta from notifications and pollsters (if available)

Currently, Ceilometer is only able to use the image_meta
structure from notifications provided by Nova, since the relevant
metadata is not written to the guests' libvirt XML files.

A new patch is available that adds the same metadata that gets
exposed in Nova notifications to libvirt XML metadata, so this
change implements reading this metadata and adding it to the
Ceilometer samples.

Since image_meta is now available from the compute pollsters,
meters.yaml has been also updated to also publish image_meta
from compute notification meter samples.

Processing for generating image_meta was also implemented when using
Nova client to discover instances (instance_discovery_method is
set to workload_partitioning), using the image metadata already
fetched using a Glance API request. This seems to work okay, but
has the disadvantages of a) only being available for ephemeral
instances (booted from image), and b) possibly being out of date
with what the instance is actually running, as the Glance image may
have been updated after the instance was launched
(the libvirt metadata contains what the instance was *actually*
configured with).

Signed-off-by: Callum Dickinson <callum.dickinson@catalystcloud.nz>
Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/nova/+/942766

source.opening_commit_message:
Add node_labels and node_taints to NodeGroup

Magnum's NodeGroup objects currently have no way to express the
Kubernetes node labels or taints that should be applied to the nodes in
a worker pool. The existing labels field stores Magnum-level
configuration (e.g. auto_scaling_enabled) rather than Kubernetes
metadata, so reusing it would be a breaking semantic change.

Add two new optional, nullable fields to NodeGroup:

* node_labels: dict of string-to-string, applied to every node in the
  group as Kubernetes node labels.
* node_taints: list of {key, value, effect} dicts, where effect must be
  one of NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, NoExecute.

Both fields are surfaced on the v1 NodeGroup REST controller for create
and PATCH, and the NodeGroup object version is bumped 1.2 -> 1.3. A new
alembic migration adds the corresponding JSON columns. Taint entries
are validated for a required key and a recognised effect; label strings
are forwarded as-is and validated by Kubernetes at registration time.
The REST API microversion is bumped to 1.13.

Storing and validating these fields is Magnum's responsibility;
honouring them is the driver's. Drivers that can apply node labels and
taints at node-registration time should do so; drivers that cannot may
ignore the fields.

APIImpact

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Change-Id: I947cb043d8f36e5fd51fdd9c166a6a7c56d6d057
Signed-off-by: Sam Morrison <sorrison@gmail.com>
source.subject: Add node_labels and node_taints to NodeGroup

targets.commit_message:
Add node label and taint support to nodegroups

Magnum's NodeGroup resource gained two new optional fields in API
microversion 1.13: node_labels (dict of string-to-string) and
node_taints (list of {key, value, effect} dicts). Expose them through
the client.

Set them at creation time:

  openstack coe nodegroup create \
      --node-labels workload=gpu \
      --node-taints nectar.org.au/unreachable:NoSchedule \
      <cluster> <name>

And update them on an existing nodegroup with new flags on the update
command:

  openstack coe nodegroup update \
      --node-labels workload=gpu \
      --node-taints workload=gpu:NoSchedule \
      <cluster> <nodegroup>

Both flags accept comma- or semicolon-separated values and may be
repeated. A new handle_taints() helper parses KEY[=VALUE]:EFFECT
entries (the VALUE is optional) into the list-of-dicts shape expected
by the API and raises CommandError for malformed input or unrecognised
effects. The update command sends each field as a string-serialised
JSON patch value, which the API deserializes, and an empty value clears
the field. node_labels and node_taints are added to CREATION_ATTRIBUTES
and to the NODEGROUP_ATTRIBUTES display list.

Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/magnum/+/988899
Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Change-Id: Id5e9b6593e83b9ffe856e73823bf418b1a66321f
Signed-off-by: Sam Morrison <sorrison@gmail.com>

source.opening_commit_message:
Add DPLL pin priority enforcement script

Add change_network_card_pin_config.py that applies DPLL pin
priorities and states via pynetlink on zl3073x hardware.

Pin group matching logic (single place to update for new boards):
- gnss: PinType.GNSS + INPUT
- synce: PinType.SYNCE + INPUT
- ptp: PinType.EXT + INPUT + board_label contains SDP_TIMESYNC
- ext: PinType.EXT + INPUT + non-empty label, excludes SDP_TIMESYNC

Unlabeled pins are never modified by any group.

Also adds the platform::ptpinstance::dpll_pin_config puppet class
that writes the JSON config and invokes the script after gnss_state
in the runtime manifest chain.

Features:
- Graceful skip on non-GNR-D (exit 0 if no zl3073x pins found)
- Partial failure returns rc=1, other groups still applied
- Sets priority on both EEC and PPS DPLL devices

targets.commit_message:
collectd: add holdover severity escalation for dpll-mgr

Extend the dpll-mgr holdover alarm to escalate severity as holdover
progresses through tiers (ho_0 to ho_3). Include the ITU-T clockClass
in the alarm reason text, read directly from dpll-mgr status.json.

Severity mapping:
- ho_0: WARNING  (fresh holdover, OCXO within spec)
- ho_1: MINOR   (drift accumulating)
- ho_2: MAJOR   (extended holdover, action needed)
- ho_3: CRITICAL (beyond rated holdover)

Changes:
- Add DPLL_MGR_HOLDOVER_SEVERITY mapping (tier → FM severity)
- Add _dpll_mgr_holdover_level state tracking (detect tier transitions)
- Update _check_dpll_mgr_state(): severity escalation on tier change,
  boot grace check on holdover branch, reset raised flag to force
  FM in-place update via set_fault()
- Read clock_class from status.json for alarm reason text
- Add collectd log with level/severity/clockClass/duration per
  transition
